title: Mississippi No. 1 sweet potatoes bring mostly $22 to $24 a carton ahead of Thanksgiving
excerpt: USDA’s Nov. 23 report puts most 40-pound cartons of No. 1 orange sweet potatoes at 55 to 60 cents a pound before freight. No. 2 cartons brought less.
locality: Mississippi shipping points, with Louisiana comparison and Pontotoc County agricultural research context.

facts.statement: Mississippi’s U.S. No. 1 orange sweet potatoes sold mostly for $22 to $24 per 40-pound carton at shipping points as Thanksgiving week began. That works out to 55 to 60 cents a pound before freight. The U.S. Department of Agriculture described demand as fairly good and the market as about steady in its Nov. 23 report.
facts.evidence: Read the Mississippi block, orange types, U.S. One, in the dated Nov. 23 report. Divided the endpoints of the most common range by 40.
facts.statistics: 40 pounds. $22–$24 divided by 40 equals $0.55–$0.60 per pound.

facts.evidence: Checked U.S. Two, ungraded jumbo and U.S. One separately. The two lower ranges are the most common prices. The last range is the full reported No. 1 spread.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi’s U.S. No. 1 orange sweet potatoes sold mostly for $22 to $24 per 40-pound carton at shipping points as Thanksgiving week began. That works out to 55 to 60 cents a pound before freight. The U.S. Department of Agriculture described demand as fairly good and the market as about steady in its Nov. 23 report.

Grade made a difference of several dollars a box. Mississippi U.S. No. 2 sweet potatoes sold mostly for $13.50 to $15 per 40 pounds. Jumbo sweet potatoes without a grade mark brought mostly $14 to $15.50 for the same weight. The full reported range for No. 1 cartons was $21 to $25.50.

Louisiana’s No. 1 orange sweet potatoes brought $23.50 to $24 a carton, near the top of the usual Mississippi range. USDA tracks open-market sales by the first handlers of the crop. The prices describe what the boxes brought at the shipping point, before transportation to market. Grocery-store prices and individual Pontotoc County farm sales are outside the scope of the report.

Pontotoc County’s role in that market starts before there is a crop to sell. Mississippi State’s Pontotoc Ridge-Flatwoods Branch produces virus-free plant material and slips for sweet potato growers across the Southeast. The university identifies it as one of six sweet potato clean-seed centers in the country.
